output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The initialSupply is added to the target's balance without a check, allowing the owner to set the balance of an arbitrary user to any value.
The mintToken function has a wrong logic vulnerability. The initialSupply is added to the target's balance without a check, allowing the owner to set the balance of an arbitrary user to any value.

output_list.vulnerability: The buy function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The amount is calculated as msg.value * buyRate, where buyRate can be very large, causing the multiplication to wrap around and become very small, allowing attackers to buy large amounts of the token for very little ether.

The buy function has a wrong logic vulnerability. The buyRate can be set to a very large value, causing the amount to become very small due to an integer overflow, allowing attackers to buy large amounts of the token for very little ether.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The balanceOf[msg.sender] -= _value; can underflow if _value is larger than balanceOf[msg.sender], causing it to wrap around and become a very large value, allowing attackers to cause a denial of service.
